one_hop_nodes.reconstructed_theorem:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with its normed additive commutative group structure, Borel measurable structure, and canonical Lebesgue/Haar volume measure lambda. Dimension zero is included. Let V : E -> R and alpha, eta : R. Assume alpha > 0, eta > 0, V is globally C^2, and for every x,v in E the directional bilinear Hessian satisfies D^2 V(x)[v,v] >= alpha ||v||^2. Let f : E -> R be any globally C^1 function whose nonzero support has compact closure; f may have either sign.

Use the actual normalized exponential tilt T_rho(q) from the ambient definition context: when the exponential weight is integrable, its density relative to rho is exp(q) / integral exp(q) d rho. Define the exact measures
mu = T_lambda(x -> -V(x)),
R_y = T_mu(x -> -||x-y||^2 / (2 eta)),
S_y = T_lambda(u -> -V((1/2)(y+u)) - ||y-u||^2 / (8 eta)).
Here (1/2)(y+u) is real scalar multiplication of the vector y+u; these measures are defined at every parameter y, using the literal reference measures displayed above.

Then both of the following hold:
(1) For every y in E, S_y equals the measurable pushforward of R_y by the exact affine map x -> 2x-y. Equivalently, for every Borel set A in E, S_y(A) = R_y({x in E : 2x-y is in A}). The inverse affine map is u -> (1/2)(u+y).
(2) The whole mean function M : E -> R, M(y) = integral f(u) d S_y(u), with the real Bochner integral, is globally C^1: its Frechet derivative exists everywhere and is continuous.

The two conclusions form a conjunction. No probability, partition positivity/finiteness, integrability, law-equality, conditional-version, derivative-continuity, upper Hessian, upper step-size, normalizer or closed-gradient certificate is an additional caller premise. No derivative formula, rough-observer extension, trajectory, convergence/mixing, numerical-error, oracle-cost or complexity conclusion is asserted.
